question: Which of the following is detected by gustatory receptors in our body?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Taste**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• **Gustatory receptors** are specialized sensory cells responsible for the perception of **taste**. These receptors are primarily located on the **tongue**, though they are also found on the **soft palate**, **epiglottis**, and **pharynx**.
 
• These receptors are clustered into structures known as **taste buds**, which are embedded within **papillae** (small bumps on the tongue surface). Each taste bud contains **50 to 100 taste receptor cells**.
 
• The primary function of gustatory receptors is to detect **chemical substances** dissolved in **saliva**. These chemicals (tastants) bind to the receptors, triggering **nerve impulses** that are sent to the **brain** for processing.
 
• Human gustatory receptors can distinguish between **five primary tastes**: **Sweet**, **Sour**, **Salty**, **Bitter**, and **Umami** (savory).
